business_problem: Yingzhicheng wanted to turn a fragmented electronics supply chain into a transparent, digital, end-to-end operating model for small and midsize hardware companies. Its earlier web platform offered limited upstream and downstream collaboration, weak mobile ordering, poor data visibility, and little support for intelligent quotation, capacity prediction, or coordinated manufacturing execution.
solution_summary: Yingzhicheng rebuilt its electronics industry platform around Alibaba's cloud and DingTalk ecosystem so supply, manufacturing, and delivery data could move through one digital chain. The company uses MaxCompute for industrial-scale data processing and pairs it with dedicated DingTalk as the unified operating entry point for upstream and downstream enterprises. Connectors synchronize ERP, MES, PLM, and SRM data, while cloud-native K8s, microservices, distributed technology, and service mesh underpin SaaS-style CRM, BOSS, ERP, and MES services. On top of that foundation, Yingzhicheng applies BOM algorithms, machine learning, NLP, and industry models to power intelligent quotation, cost optimization, supply-demand matching, PCBA delivery, and full production-lifecycle transparency. ACR-based image sharing lets the team roll out region-wide updates quickly, so factories can run cloud MES or private deployments with the same digital workflow and AI-driven planning logic.

solution_components.name: MaxCompute
solution_components.role: Processes industrial data used for BOM intelligence, pricing, demand matching, and manufacturing analytics.

solution_components.name: Dedicated DingTalk
solution_components.role: Serves as the unified entry point where upstream and downstream enterprises collaborate and exchange operational data.

solution_components.name: Cloud-native K8s platform
solution_components.role: Runs Yingzhicheng's SaaS CRM, ERP, and MES services on a scalable microservices foundation.

solution_components.name: ACR
solution_components.role: Distributes shared images so MES and ERP deployments can be updated quickly across regions.

data_flow: BOM, procurement, production, and fulfillment data flows from upstream and downstream systems through DingTalk connectors into the cloud platform, where MaxCompute and Yingzhicheng's industry models process the data for quotation, recommendation, and manufacturing decisions. Those decisions are then executed through K8s-hosted ERP and MES services, while factory and logistics status is fed back into the same platform for real-time lifecycle visibility.
business_outcome: Yingzhicheng turned its electronics supply-chain platform into a transparent digital manufacturing network that can support intelligent quotation, supply-demand coordination, and end-to-end production visibility. The cloud architecture gave customers mobile and real-time access to orders, inventory, manufacturing progress, and logistics while letting Yingzhicheng reuse AI models and cloud MES or ERP images across many different hardware and factory scenarios.
architecture_clues: Dedicated DingTalk is used as the operational front door for all upstream and downstream participants.
AI capabilities are applied to BOM understanding, quotation, cost optimization, and capacity matching rather than only dashboard analytics.
The service stack is built on cloud-native K8s, microservices, distributed technology, and service mesh.
ACR image sharing enables fast regional rollout of MES and ERP instances for customer-specific deployments.
